intro.title: Error Boundary
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React component called an Error Boundary to catch and handle JavaScript errors in your application. You will learn how to use the componentDidCatch lifecycle method to gracefully display a fallback UI when an error occurs, preventing the entire app from crashing. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and class components with proper type definitions. By the end, you'll have a reusable Error Boundary that improves your app's resilience and user experience.
intro.usecase: Error Boundaries are essential in production React applications where any component failure could crash the entire user interface. In dashboard applications with multiple independent widgets (charts, data tables, status panels), an error in one widget shouldn't break the entire dashboard. Similarly, in e-commerce product pages with complex interactive elements (image galleries, reviews, recommendations), Error Boundaries prevent a single malfunctioning component from making the whole page unusable. This pattern allows developers to gracefully handle failures while maintaining core functionality and providing helpful error messages to users.
